explicit_definitions_given: Primary substance: ultimate subject of predication
Potentiality: real capacity grounded in nature

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Systematically addresses objections to Aristotle (e.g., Third Man, substratum problem) and critiques Plato
objections_raised: Plato's participation is metaphorical and unexplained
Plato's Forms lead to Third Man regress
Plato fails to identify a coherent substratum
Plato's dualism shatters the unity of the person
Plato's recollection requires a heavy metaphysical burden

epistemic_stance_and_voice.certainty_language_frequency: High - uses terms like 'decisive', 'unequivocally yes', 'profoundly different'

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Textual exegesis, logical argument, thought experiments, comparative analysis

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Analytic metaphysics, history of philosophy, Aristotelian realism
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Aristotelian - favors immanent realism, hylomorphism, and teleological naturalism
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Problem of change, predication, substratum, participation vs. actuality

structural_organization.structure_type: Comparative problem-solution-evaluation with four parts: (I) framing, (II) Plato's view and critique, (III) Aristotle's view and defense, (IV) comparative evaluation

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that Aristotle's ontology of primary substance, accidents, potentiality, and actuality provides a coherent and non-metaphorical account of change, whereas Plato's theory of Forms and participation fails to explain the unity of the substratum and leads to regress and dualism.
